explanation: A king of Judah who reigned from 735 to 715 BC and did many evil things in God's sight.
The capital city of the kingdom of Judah, an important religious and political center for the Israelite people.
The capital of Syria, a powerful city-state in ancient times and an enemy of the kingdom of Judah.
The king of Syria who attacked Judah together with Pekah, the king of Israel, in an attempt to force Ahas to join their coalition against Assyria.
The king of Israel who allied himself with Rezin, the king of Syria, to attack Judah and force Ahas to join their coalition against Assyria.
The king of Assyria whom Ahas sought help from to protect his kingdom from attacks by Israel and Syria.
A powerful empire in ancient Mesopotamia that dominated the region and was a threat to both Israel and Syria.
A structure where offerings and prayers were presented to God or gods as part of religious rituals.
A water source near Jerusalem that Ahas protected by building a tunnel to lead the water into the city.
The son of Ahas and his successor as king of Judah, known for his piety and reforms to bring the people back to God.
